work.name: Rayca Precision
work.summary: I gained hands-on experience designing and deploying an AI-driven virtual screening pipeline integrating generative modeling, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate over 300,000 compounds. I built automated, high-throughput Python workflows for protein preparation, DiffDock/AutoDock Vina docking, GROMACS post-simulation analysis, binding free energy calculations, and ADMET filtering. This work led to the prioritization of 12 antagonist candidates for synthesis and experimental validation while strengthening my expertise in scalable structure-based drug discovery and AI-enabled molecular design.

work.name: University of Texas at Dallas
work.summary: I conduct research in computational chemistry, applying molecular dynamics simulations and quantum mechanical (QM/MM) methods to investigate enzyme mechanisms and mutation-driven structural changes at the atomic level. My work integrates free-energy calculations, bioinformatics analysis, and machine learning to understand disease-associated mutations and biomolecular function. This research has strengthened my expertise in physics-based modeling, high-performance computing, and data-driven analysis of complex biological systems.
